ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The moon in water is the moon’s visible reflection on a water surface, not another moon that can be taken from the water.
EvidenceBody: The Record of Xiangyan Xixin pictures the moon disk suspended in the blue sky and its round image falling into the ocean; the Records of the Source-Mirror describes the water-moon beside a mirror image and explicitly calls the constructed image provisional rather than real. Zhiyan Liaojue says that the bright moon casts its image over a clear pool while neither water nor moon intends the relation, and then speaks of forgetting both. Hongzhi’s verse retains the image as a moonlit waterscape. A previous temple-name substring has been removed because it names a place, not the reflection.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Chan records use the reflection both as a named image and inside questions, rebukes, and paired image formulas; the sky-disk/ocean-image clause makes the ordinary referent explicit.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: Not every 水月 is an unreality claim: Hongzhi’s 水月茫茫 is a waterscape. The removed the Water-Moon Temple name hit was lexical contamination.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: The temple name is a different lexical item and has been excluded; landscape and comparison uses retain the same reflected-moon referent.
